then.text: You've a job here any time, love. Pay's terrible, but you can eat the mistakes.
You beat Liam at pulling? He's been here three summers! Right, that's your training done.
Here's how it goes: boil the sugar and glucose to a hard crack, pour it on the slab, then colour some red and pull the rest until it goes white and shiny.

The letters are built by hand, in red, each one as a long fat bar packed with white, set round the middle like a stick of seaside rock in cross-section. Then the whole lump's rolled and pulled out thin, and every inch says BLACKPOOL.
Here's your wages. In rock. Don't eat it all at once. You will, but don't.
Go on, take on Liam. He's over by the pulling hook, showing off.

else.text: Short-handed, I am! It's switch-on week and the whole town wants rock. Can you pull sugar?
No? You'll learn. First, see Liam, my apprentice. Beat him and you've earned your apron.

then.text: Fair play. I'll stick to wrapping. Wrapping can't beat you in a battle.
Maureen says you're the new apprentice? Over my dead sugar. Rock-pulling battle! Loser does the washing up.
Aw, man. Go on then, tell Maureen. I'll get the washing-up gloves.

else.text: Mind the slab, it's hot. Boiled sugar sticks to everything. Especially eyebrows.
